Codex TUI performance: A:oracle

baseline-original, load-gated: official codex 0.170.0 release, single binary, alt-screen, 120x40 - started 2026-11-18T13:07:38+00:00, finished 2026-11-18T13:48:47+00:00

What is compared

Same Codex core and the same kind of fake model (Codex's own MockResponsesServer, one server and one fresh CODEX_HOME per run, analytics off, no network); both run in a pty at the scenario size with TERM=xterm-256color and the driver's VT model; only the frontend differs. Everything is black box through the pty: CPU and RSS from proc_pidinfo every 100 ms and wait4 rusage, frames are DEC 2026 pairs (read bursts when absent), a key is "visible" when the VT model shows it in the screen (a DEC 2026 update held longer than 150 ms counts as visible). The VT model is a model, not a GPU terminal: byte volume is the proxy for terminal cost.

N = 15 rounds, interleaved (single binary), a preflight launch per binary discarded. Machine: MacBookPro18,2, 10 CPUs, 64.0 GB, macOS-26.6.2-arm64-arm-64bit-Mach-O, power: Now drawing from 'AC Power'; rustc 1.99.1 (58cf8f9c3 2026-10-13); driver commit 3b850b3e1.

Load (1-min, before each run): median 6.1, max 32.7, gate 15.0 (1.5 x CPUs); 15 of 105 runs started above the gate (taken with --measure-only; the shared machine was busy: absolute numbers carry that noise, the interleaving keeps A and B comparable). Start 7.5, end 7.0.

Screen mode: A:oracle: alt-screen. Frame source: sync.
